propositions: merge.ours.driver is set per-clone in init.py but never committed, so reconcile-bridge.yml runner lacks the driver definition and git silently falls back to 3-way text merge of .bridge_state/* instead of local-wins merge
reconcile-bridge.yml performs bare git worktree add without calling rebar init, unlike reconcile-bridge-canary.yml which calls rebar init and already obtains the driver via _merge_ours_unit
undefined merge driver on the runner causes large JSON blobs to be 3-way merged instead of taking local version, breaking merge=ours semantics and creating fragility for blob:none reconverge path
reconcile-bridge.yml must set merge.ours.driver=true for the tickets worktree before any merge step to ensure local-wins behavior and prevent lazy blob materialization faults
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml does not require changes because rebar init already configures the driver, providing a regression guard against scope creep
